description: boto3 client created inside handler function body
impact: 50–300ms latency added per warm invocation due to new SDK session
fix_summary: Move to module level or use lazy-init pattern

description: boto3 client or resource created without botocore Config
impact: Reduced connection reuse and weaker retry/timeout behavior
fix_summary: Add Config(tcp_keepalive=True, max_pool_connections=10, retries=...) to all boto3 calls

description: botocore Config is not imported even though boto3 is used
impact: Prevents standard Lambda client tuning from being applied
fix_summary: Add: from botocore.config import Config

description: Logger level is hardcoded instead of controlled by environment
impact: Requires redeploy to change verbosity; can increase logging overhead in hot paths
fix_summary: Replace with: logger.setLevel(os.environ.get('LOG_LEVEL', 'INFO'))

description: Handler does not emit a structured invocation log at startup
impact: Harder CloudWatch correlation and slower per-invocation troubleshooting
fix_summary: Add: logger.info(json.dumps({'event': 'lambda_invoked', 'function': context.function_name}))

description: Paginator used without a TTL cache check
impact: 100–500ms of repeated list API latency paid on warm invocations
fix_summary: Wrap paginator results in a module-level TTL cache dict

description: AWS API call appears inside a loop body
impact: N+1 latency and cost proportional to item count
fix_summary: Batch requests or cache per-item lookups

description: boto3 client or resource hardcodes a region string
impact: Breaks portability across regions
fix_summary: Omit region_name or use os.environ.get('AWS_REGION')

description: Broad exception handler before boto3-specific handling
impact: Obscures AWS-specific failures
fix_summary: Catch ClientError and BotoCoreError before broad except

description: AWS SDK client instantiated inside the handler function
impact: New TLS connection and credential refresh on every warm invocation
fix_summary: Move client instantiation to module scope (outside the handler)

description: AWS SDK for JavaScript v2 detected — in maintenance mode
impact: Larger bundle, slower cold start, no active feature development
fix_summary: Migrate to AWS SDK v3: @aws-sdk/client-* packages

description: No HTTP keepAlive agent on SDK client — connections not reused
impact: New TLS handshake per SDK call, adds 50–150ms per warm invocation
fix_summary: Add NodeHttpHandler with Agent({ keepAlive: true }) from @smithy/node-http-handler

description: AWS SDK client without explicit maxAttempts
impact: Transient failures may not be retried reliably
fix_summary: Set maxAttempts: 3 in client config

description: Async handler without try/catch — unhandled rejections silently fail
impact: Errors are swallowed, CloudWatch shows no error, debugging is impossible
fix_summary: Wrap handler body in try { ... } catch (err) { console.error(err); throw err; }

description: Full SDK v2 import increases deployment package size
impact: Larger bundle size, slower cold starts
fix_summary: Use per-service SDK v3 imports: import { S3Client } from '@aws-sdk/client-s3'

description: Hardcoded region string in SDK client config
impact: Breaks portability across regions
fix_summary: Use process.env.AWS_REGION

description: No structured JSON log at handler start
impact: Harder CloudWatch correlation
fix_summary: Add: console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: 'lambda_invoked', function: context.functionName }))

description: AWS SDK client created inside handler function — not reused on warm invocations
impact: New TLS connection and credential refresh on every warm invocation
fix_summary: Move to package-level var + init()

description: AWS SDK for Go v1 detected — in maintenance mode
impact: Missing context support, worse API, not actively developed
fix_summary: Migrate to github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2

description: No custom http.Transport — uses Go default with limited connection pooling
impact: Only 2 idle connections per host; new TLS handshake on each SDK call under load
fix_summary: Create http.Client with custom Transport (KeepAlive:30s, MaxIdleConns:100)

description: SDK client not declared in package-level var block
impact: Client may not be preserved across warm invocations
fix_summary: Declare as var and initialise in init()

description: Log level not controlled by LOG_LEVEL environment variable
impact: Cannot change verbosity without redeployment
fix_summary: Read os.Getenv("LOG_LEVEL") and configure logger accordingly

description: No structured JSON log at handler start
impact: Harder CloudWatch correlation
fix_summary: Add structured log with function name and request ID

description: AWS SDK client instantiated inside handleRequest() — recreated every invocation
impact: New connection pool and credential refresh on every invocation
fix_summary: Declare as private static final and build once at class loading time

description: AWS SDK for Java v1 detected (com.amazonaws.*) — in maintenance mode
impact: Older API, worse performance, not actively developed
fix_summary: Migrate to software.amazon.awssdk.* (SDK v2)

description: SDK client built without explicit HTTP client configuration
impact: Default connection pool and timeout settings may not suit Lambda workloads
fix_summary: Add ApacheHttpClient.builder().maxConnections(50).connectionTimeout(...) to client builder

description: No private static final SDK client field found
impact: Client likely recreated per invocation, wasting connection setup time
fix_summary: Add: private static final XxxClient CLIENT = XxxClient.builder()...build();

description: SDK client built without explicit retry policy
impact: Transient failures may not be retried reliably
fix_summary: Add .overrideConfiguration(c -> c.retryPolicy(RetryPolicy.builder().numRetries(3).build()))

description: Java handler does not implement CRaC interface for SnapStart
impact: Misses opportunity to eliminate cold start entirely on Java 21
fix_summary: Implement org.crac.Resource and register with Core.getGlobalContext()

description: No structured log at the start of handleRequest()
impact: Harder CloudWatch correlation
fix_summary: Add: context.getLogger().log("{\"event\":\"lambda_invoked\"}");
